judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3 (rank 3) Reading and Phonics / Shared Reading Skill statements about using visual cues, so the within-grade Term order governs direction. The second SFI sits under TERM 2 (identity scope 'grade=grade 3|term=term 2'), stating 'Uses visual cues to identify the purpose of advertisements and the intended audience'. The first SFI sits under TERM 4 (identity scope 'grade=grade 3|term=term 4') and extends the same visual-cue reading skill to graphical texts generally and adds a new critical layer: 'starts to analyse text for attitudes and assumptions, e.g., "Who is this advertisement meant to appeal to? Why do you think this?"'. That is substantive deepening (from identifying stated purpose/audience to inferring underlying attitudes and assumptions), and its LCs ('Uses visual cues to read graphical texts'; 'Starts to analyse text for attitudes and assumptions') presuppose the Term 2 purpose/audience identification. Direction is therefore earlier Term 2 (second) to later Term 4 (first), which is the only valid within-grade developmental direction here. However, the evidence gives no pair-specific developmental dependency or ordering: both are same-grade, same-term statements and neither statement text nor its Learning Components ('Reads own writing', 'Starts to correct errors' vs 'Spells common words correctly') shows one as an expanded or prerequisite capability of the other, so no buildsTowards direction is justified. The substantive coherence (both develop early word recognition and print engagement within the same Grade 1 Reading and Phonics programme, with shared reading of high-frequency printed text reinforcing sight words) supports symmetric relatesTo. The first requires fine visual discrimination tied to emergent literacy — distinguishing shapes of letters and words, sorting identical objects, and picking out the odd picture from a nearly identical sequence with an explanation. The second requires locating an object hidden among other classroom items and then guiding peers to items with simple directions. These are complementary applications of attending to visual detail within the same visual-cues strand, but the second is not a deepening or extension of the first: searching for a concealed object among dissimilar items does not rely on discriminating near-identical letter/word shapes, and the oral direction-giving component (LC 'Guides peers to items using simple directions'; tags 'directions', 'position', 'speaking') is an unrelated expressive capability with no precursor in the Term 2 statement. Lexical evidence is generic (shared sfi tokens 'a', 'and'; shared LC tag token 'visual'; jaccard 0.02–0.09) and shared hierarchy, grade rank, or sub-strand alone cannot license buildsTowards. judgment.rationale: Both Skills are Grade 3 (rank 3, resolved coordinates), Term 1, Reading and Phonics, sub-strand 'Phonic Activities three times a week for 15 minutes', printed as sibling bullets in the same table row (row=3, window 43, page 110). The first is recognition of consonant digraphs (sh-, -sh, ch-, -ch, th-, -th, wh-) in initial and final position; the second is recognition that some sounds are represented by several different spelling choices, exemplified by vowel patterns (play/pain/plate; feet/read/key; boat/blow/note; tiger/like/sigh/fly). They are substantively coherent complementary phonics skills: both concern how written graphemes map to single sounds and both feed the same Term 1 decoding/spelling work, so this is meaningful instructional coherence rather than generic repetition. However, the evidence does not establish that proficiency with the fixed set of consonant digraphs materially supports success with the distinct vowel-spelling-alternatives generalisation; the graphemes, target sounds and conceptual insight differ, and neither statement broadens, deepens or increases the complexity of the other. Same-grade, same-term development requires substantive extension evidence, which is absent, and bullet order within the printed row is not progression evidence. Shared LC tag 'phonics', the 'recognises'/'of' token overlap and trigram overlap, shared ancestry and page proximity were not treated as relational evidence. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both endpoints and all four shared ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the bounded statement text, resolved coordinates and hierarchy supplied.

Confidence is moderate because each endpoint has 24 omitted source-evidence items and truncated LC evidence, and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context that must be inspected before stronger inference.

Nomination support is weak (LC tag jaccard 0.17 on 'sequence'/'story', SFI token overlap only on stopwords, rank_gap 0 rated 'weak'), so no developmental dependency is established and relatesTo is the correct symmetric judgment with null direction; canonical endpoint order is unchanged.
